evidence: In the heart of Hanoi's Old Quarter, a culinary icon stands out amidst the bustling streets: Ly Quoc Su Pho Restaurant, a name that echoes the spirit of the imperial capital. This esteemed eatery, situated on the eponymous street, has been a staple of traditional Northern Pho flavor since the subsidy period.

In the heart of Hanoi's Old Quarter, a culinary icon stands out amidst the bustling streets: Ly Quoc Su Pho Restaurant, a name that echoes the spirit of the imperial capital. This esteemed eatery, situated on the eponymous street, has been a staple of traditional Northern Pho flavor since the subsidy period.

As you step into the restaurant, you're immediately struck by the vibrant orange signboard and the stainless steel preparation counter, a beacon of culinary excellence. The pièce de résistance is the giant nước lèo pot, billowing with thick white smoke, situated next to a glass display case filled with hanging pinkish beef.
